title: Efficient Identity and Position Graph Embedding via Spectral-Based Random Feature Aggregation

problem.claim: GNN-based graph embedding methods may not clearly preserve identity or position properties and may have low efficiency and scalability.

gap.claim: It is unclear which graph property most GNN-based methods capture, while feature extraction and training can be time- and space-consuming.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes random feature aggregation for efficient identity and position embedding.
RFA uses a parameter-free spectral-based GNN, random-noise inputs, and one feed-forward propagation to derive embeddings.
The method adds a degree-correction mechanism inspired by degree-corrected spectral clustering.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that high- and low-pass RFA variants derive informative identity and position embeddings with one feed-forward propagation and no training.
The authors report that RFA achieves a better quality-efficiency trade-off than various baselines for both identity and position embedding.
The authors report that their code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs support graph tasks through feature aggregation, and graph embedding can target node identity or position properties.
Existing GNN methods have unclear property coverage and may be inefficient or difficult to scale.
Graph spectral frequency information may characterize node identities and positions differently.
RFA combines spectral-based parameter-free propagation, random inputs, one-step embedding derivation, and degree correction.
The authors report informative embeddings and improved quality-efficiency trade-offs without training.

source_observation.claim: High- and low-frequency graph spectral information may correspond to different structural properties.

interpretation.claim: Separating frequency components can provide a principled way to target distinct embedding objectives.

application.claim: When designing graph representations, consider spectral filters matched to the structural property of interest.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this correspondence holds across all graph types or tasks.

unknowns: Datasets, baseline identities, evaluation metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not provide theoretical guarantees or detailed reproducibility conditions.
